checked_sources.source: Saha & Ramdas 2026, Non-partitioned e-detectors for nonparametric sequential change detection, arXiv:2607.28322v1
checked_sources.result: Full-paper verification. The construction needs conditionally valid s-delay e-processes for each candidate no-change law. The unweighted SR-style aggregate is an e-detector with ARL >= A and finite-horizon false-alarm bound P(tau<=m)<=m/A. The weighted aggregate with deterministic pi_s>0 summing to at most one is an e-process with global PFA <= alpha. Exact explicit implementations can cost O(t) per update and quadratic total work through horizon N. The paper's internal start-time aggregation is not a theorem that repeatedly resetting the whole detector after each alarm at the same alpha preserves global PFA.

checked_sources.source: Ramdas 2026, Universality of e-detectors for ARL control, arXiv:2608.12660v1
checked_sources.result: Primary verification that strong e-detectors imply optional-horizon control P(T_b<=sigma)<=E[sigma]/b for every data-dependent stopping horizon, while bare ARL permits eventual false alarm with probability one. The clocked formulation allows predictable exposure/cost clocks. This sharpens the distinction between ARL routing and global-PFA routing.

checked_sources.source: Dziugaite & Roy 2018, Data-dependent PAC-Bayes priors via differential privacy, NeurIPS 2018
checked_sources.result: Primary theorem-level verification that an epsilon-differentially-private prior selected from the same iid bounded-loss sample can still yield a PAC-Bayes bound holding simultaneously for all posteriors Q, with an explicit privacy/max-information penalty. This is an explicit way to charge for prior adaptation rather than requiring a fully data-independent prior, but it is static iid and not itself time-uniform/off-policy.

checked_sources.source: Tian & Ramdas 2021, Online control of the familywise error rate
checked_sources.result: Primary-source confirmation that a potentially infinite sequence of tests needs online FWER accounting to keep the probability of any false discovery over the full sequence controlled. Alpha-spending is the basic construction; adaptive improvements exist under additional assumptions. This supplies the correct accounting analogy for repeated detector resets when global no-false-alarm probability matters.

candidates_new.mechanism: Use a non-partitioned e-detector as an evidence-staleness router when no single stable pre-change distribution is known. Aggregate point-null delayed e-processes over candidate changepoints and minimize over candidate common laws instead of hard-coding one baseline partition.
candidates_new.quantitative_or_formal_evidence: Finite-sample ARL mode: E[tau]>=A and P(tau<=m)<=m/A. Global-PFA mode: with deterministic start weights summing to <=1, P(tau<infinity)<=alpha. Under stated late-change regularity the delay is first-order optimal; for canonical PFA weights the delay numerator pays log(1/alpha)+log T+2 log log(eT)+O(1).
candidates_new.scope: Single continuously running detector over a composite no-change class, with conditionally valid delayed e-process primitives. It does not by itself certify repeated whole-detector reset cycles at unchanged alpha.
candidates_new.failure_conditions: Exact all-start implementations may accumulate O(t) per-update and O(N^2) total cost; global-PFA weighting pays a late-start penalty; ARL mode allows eventual false alarm and cannot be interpreted as an ever-false-alarm probability guarantee.
candidates_new.transfer_hypothesis: For adaptive system memory routing, prefer composite unknown-baseline monitoring when a fixed calibration mean/distribution is not defensible; choose ARL or PFA semantics explicitly instead of treating them as interchangeable.
candidates_new.confidence: high for statistical component; medium for optimizer-memory transfer

candidates_new.mechanism: If an alarm causes a full detector reset and monitoring continues, treat alarm epochs as an online multiple-testing sequence. Allocate a global false-alarm budget across reset epochs (alpha_j with sum alpha_j<=alpha, or a stronger online-FWER rule) rather than restarting every epoch at the same alpha.
candidates_new.quantitative_or_formal_evidence: A single Saha-Ramdas PFA detector controls probability of ever alarming at alpha because its start-time weights sum to <=1. Online FWER work shows the analogous infinite-test guarantee requires explicit error-budget accounting across tests. Reusing the same positive alpha after each full reset has no supplied global-PFA theorem and a naive union bound diverges over infinitely many resets.
candidates_new.scope: Global probability of any false reset across a continuing sequence. This is not needed if only per-cycle ARL is the intended metric.
candidates_new.failure_conditions: Aggressive alpha spending can make later drift detection very slow. Recycling or adaptive FWER methods require their own dependence assumptions. Random alarm-time restart validity of the inner delayed e-process must also be verified separately.
candidates_new.transfer_hypothesis: Maintain a durable reset-risk ledger; only a globally budgeted alarm may trigger destructive history reset, while lower-cost warnings can remain ARL-style and non-destructive.
candidates_new.confidence: high for accounting principle; medium for exact reset implementation

candidates_new.mechanism: Replace calendar-time false-alarm budgeting with a predictable exposure/cost clock C_n=sum a_j when evidence arrives irregularly or observations have unequal diagnostic cost. Strong clocked e-processes give P(T<=sigma)<=E[C_sigma]/b.
candidates_new.quantitative_or_formal_evidence: The optional-clock theorem is exact: strong C-clocked e-process thresholding is equivalent to optional-clock false-alarm control. Predictable a_j can count samples or weighted costs rather than elapsed time.
candidates_new.scope: False-alarm accounting against predictable exposure. It does not itself choose the optimal diagnostic stream or prove downstream utility after an alarm.
candidates_new.failure_conditions: If exposure weights are chosen using forbidden future information or omit material monitoring opportunities, the clock no longer represents the intended risk budget.
candidates_new.transfer_hypothesis: For asynchronous research/evaluation pipelines, charge drift-monitor risk by actual audited evaluation exposure rather than wall-clock time.
candidates_new.confidence: high for theorem; medium for transfer

candidates_new.mechanism: When a useful PAC-Bayes prior must be learned from the same data, explicitly limit prior-data dependence with differential privacy/max-information so the subsequent bound can still hold uniformly over all posteriors Q.
candidates_new.quantitative_or_formal_evidence: For bounded iid loss and an epsilon-DP data-dependent prior P(S), with probability at least 1-delta the PAC-Bayes KL-risk bound holds for every posterior Q simultaneously, paying KL(Q||P(S))/m plus the standard confidence term and explicit epsilon-dependent max-information penalties.
candidates_new.scope: Static iid PAC-Bayes generalization, not sequential time-uniform off-policy certification and not a predictable-prior theorem.
candidates_new.failure_conditions: Strong privacy can make the prior costly/noisy to learn; repeated adaptive releases compose privacy cost; no direct theorem here turns this into a continuously updated all-time off-policy certificate.
candidates_new.transfer_hypothesis: If final audit quality materially benefits from a learned prior, use an explicit adaptation charge such as DP/max-information or a fresh split rather than silently reusing audit data to tune the prior.
candidates_new.confidence: high for theorem; medium for sequential-audit transfer

evidence_updates.update: Promoted from abstract-only to theorem-level evidence. The full paper verifies composite unknown-baseline ARL and global-PFA constructions, conditional delayed-process requirements, late-change first-order optimality under stated conditions, and explicit computational scaling in examples. The unresolved part is not baseline validity but repeated whole-detector reset semantics.

Refined into two distinct semantics. Strong e-detector/ARL monitoring gives an optional-horizon linear false-alarm bound but permits eventual false alarm; e-process/PFA monitoring reserves probability mass at infinity and is appropriate when any false destructive reset must be globally rare.

A different explicit route to data-dependent priors was verified: differential privacy/max-information can recover a bound uniform over all posteriors despite a prior learned from the same iid data. This does not close the stronger sequential predictable-prior plus time-uniform/off-policy frontier.

deferred_or_negative_evidence.lead: A global-PFA e-detector can be reset after every alarm at the same alpha indefinitely with the original guarantee unchanged.
deferred_or_negative_evidence.evidence: Not supported. The verified theorem is for one globally weighted detector. Repeated full resets create a sequence of new false-alarm opportunities; infinite-sequence FWER requires explicit error-budget accounting.
deferred_or_negative_evidence.reason: Keep whole-detector reset risk budgeted across epochs.

deferred_or_negative_evidence.lead: ARL>=A means the probability of ever making a false destructive reset is at most 1/A.
deferred_or_negative_evidence.evidence: False. Strong e-detector ARL permits eventual false alarm with probability one; its stronger finite/optional-horizon guarantee is P(T<=sigma)<=E[sigma]/A, not global PFA.
deferred_or_negative_evidence.reason: Do not conflate ARL with PFA when reset cost is irreversible.

deferred_or_negative_evidence.lead: Differentially private data-dependent priors solve the current sequential off-policy predictable-prior problem end to end.
deferred_or_negative_evidence.evidence: No. The verified theorem is iid, static and bounded-loss. It supplies a useful explicit adaptivity charge but not time-uniform adaptive-logging certification.
deferred_or_negative_evidence.reason: Retain as a component or fallback, not a completed sequential theorem.

deferred_or_negative_evidence.lead: A direct vector-valued off-policy confidence sequence under adaptive logging and adaptive candidate selection is established by the sources checked in this run.
deferred_or_negative_evidence.evidence: No direct theorem was found. Scalar off-policy confidence sequences and general vector martingale/confidence-set results remain separate lines.
deferred_or_negative_evidence.reason: Do not claim joint multivariate off-policy certification yet.

frontier: Formalize repeated-reset semantics for the composite non-partitioned detector: prove or falsify conditional validity when the whole detector is reinitialized at an alarm-time stopping time, and quantify how alpha-spending versus a nonreset global detector changes detection delay.

Search for a sequential/time-uniform PAC-Bayes or e-process theorem that permits data-dependent priors with an explicit max-information/privacy/conditional-information charge while remaining simultaneous over all posterior choices under adaptive logging.

Find a direct vector-valued off-policy confidence sequence/e-process under adaptive logging and adaptive candidate selection; otherwise derive a conservative construction from scalar e-processes with explicit multiplicity accounting.
Quantify computationally safe pruning for non-partitioned all-start detectors: identify finite-sample-valid pruning or mixture-lower-bound schemes and measure delay versus O(N^2) exact evaluation.

Model the decision cost of false memory reset versus stale-memory retention and select ARL, PFA, or exposure-clock semantics based on the actual loss function rather than one universal detector metric.
Continue heavy-tail robustification of the diagnostic and off-policy layers separately before combining guarantees.

actions_taken_instead_of_stopping: Upgraded the non-partitioned e-detector lead from abstract-level to theorem/proof-level verification.
Separated internal start-time aggregation from repeated whole-detector reset semantics instead of silently equating them.
Added a global reset-risk accounting candidate using online FWER logic.
Added exposure-clock monitoring and a data-dependent-prior route with explicit privacy/max-information cost.
Searched for direct vector-valued off-policy confidence sequences and retained the absence as an open frontier rather than fabricating a combined theorem.

exact_next_action: First, inspect finite-sample-valid pruning/mixture approximations for all-start e-detectors and quantify the delay-compute tradeoff against exact O(N^2) evaluation. In parallel, search for a time-uniform PAC-Bayes/e-process theorem that allows a data-dependent prior with an explicit privacy/max-information or conditional-information charge and is simultaneous over adaptive posterior choices under adaptive logging.
